name: map-filter-reduce
axis: higher-order functions: a callback-heavy map/filter/reduce pipeline over a 20M-element array, in three spellings (builtin methods / hand-written loops building the same intermediates / one fused loop)
notes: Phase A uses each language's builtin higher-order methods (VL: xs.map(f).filter(g) + std:array reduce; JS: map/filter/reduce; Rust: iter().map().collect() / filter().collect() / fold(); Python: list(map())/list(filter())/functools.reduce). Rust's phase A collects into a Vec at each stage rather than fusing lazily, so it allocates exactly what phase B does. Phase B rebuilds the same two intermediate arrays with hand-written while loops; phase C fuses everything into one loop with no intermediates. All three print the same total (equivalence self-check). THE FINDING — per-phase, n=20M, with the array-build cost (phase 'base') subtracted: Rust A 0.038s / B 0.044s / C 0.015s; V8 A 0.270s / B 0.343s / C 0.047s; VL A 0.631s / B 0.314s / C 0.040s. VL is the ONLY one of the three where reaching for the builtin costs you: A/B is 0.86x in Rust, 0.79x in V8, and 2.01x in VL. VL's hand-written loop (B) actually BEATS V8's (0.314 vs 0.343) and its fused loop (C) beats V8's too (0.040 vs 0.047) — the whole VL deficit on this benchmark is in the builtin methods' callback dispatch. `vl build -O3` cuts the whole program from 1.011s to 0.583s and phase A from 0.804s to 0.270s. Totals at n=20M: rust 0.143s, VL 1.019s, deno 1.080s, python(2M) 0.741s. Scale-verified 10M->20M: rust 2.03x, deno 1.97x (after subtracting ~0.34s startup+JIT), VL 1.98x, python 1M->2M 2.04x. Python's N is 1/10.

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 110ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 6% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
